title: Disagreeing with stakeholders on hosted vs. self-hosted LLMs
relatedProject: CityU AI Hub - RAG Chat Systems
situation: [confirm: crafted scenario. Verify or replace.] When planning CityU's RAG chat systems, some stakeholders wanted to use a hosted frontier-model API for answer quality. I favored self-hosting open models (Gemma via Ollama) for cost control and to keep institutional data in-house.
task: Reach a decision that served the university, not my preference, and support it fully once made.
action: Instead of arguing in principle, I proposed a short bake-off: the same RAG pipeline, the same evaluation questions, a hosted model versus quantized Gemma on EC2, tracked in MLflow on answer quality, latency and projected monthly cost [confirm: whether a comparison was actually run]. I presented the results neutrally, including where the hosted model was clearly better, and laid out the data-governance implications for leadership.
result: We went with [confirm: the outcome, e.g., self-hosted for internal content with a hosted model for some use cases], and I committed fully to the decision. The quantized-deployment findings became part of my symposium talks. What I learned: when you disagree, propose an experiment, present the evidence honestly even when it cuts against you, and once the decision is made, own it.
